BMW Ponzi

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How did BMW Melrose Arch sell dozens of luxury cars through a Ponzi scheme?

Unique Selling Point:
According to the Dealer Principal BMW Melrose Arch sold "hundreds" of cars through a dodgy cash back, dealer assist scheme which was linked to a non-existent oil company in Dubai. If customers were creditworthy and had a trade-in, their new, luxury cars would pay for themselves.
When the Reserve Bank identified QSG as a Ponzi scheme and the Asset Forfeiture Unit froze R71 million in QSG's funds, the hundreds of BMW owners were no longer able to make the exorbitant payments on their new cars.

Summary:
This "special offer" was only available through BMW Melrose Arch, and only one salesman was doing the deals: Justin Lineveldt. The scheme involved inflating the invoices for the car finance by as much as possible. Trade-ins were marked up to three times their value, extras were charged for on paper, but not added to the cars; the higher the finance amount, the higher the "cash-back" deal. The "cash-back" portion was then invested in QSG, which was ostensibly doing business with an oil company in Dubai. The so-called interest on this investment would then be paid to an account at Mercantile Bank, which would then make the car payments at Wesbank or BMW Auto Finance.

Further information:
The cash-back deal was the brainchild of Daanie Delportt, a former second-hand car dealer who bought a car through Justin Lineveldt. Daanie became the self-styled Marketing Director for QSG and found hundreds of potential customers which he sent to Justin at Melrose Arch. On asking the Melrose Arch Dealer Principal if the deal was legitimate, customers were given reassurance that nothing was wrong. Daanie is also a part-time Christian preacher who convinced several customers that the Lord was on their side and rewarding them with this special deal.

BMW Melrose Arch has recently closed down, but was owned by Justin Divaris - owner of BMW Hyde Auto and BMW Sandton Isle. Justin is building an 8000m2 "candy store for supercars" in Melrose Arch. This R2 billion building will include Rolls Royce, Aston Martin, McLaren and a Marriott Hotel. This means the Sandton Isle site will become a BMW super centre.

Press Release:


Luxury Vehicle Ponzi Scam
How did a car dealer sell luxury vehicles to people who could never afford them? Carte Blanche investigates how one high-end car dealer had hundreds of people fooled with a bogus cash-back dealer-assist investment scheme linked to a non-existent oil company in Dubai. Now his clients have been left stranded, and in debt, to pay off these expensive vehicles.


Script:


BMW PONZI

V/O: It’s the brand that most South Africans aspire to, and when a too-good-to-be-true deal was dangled within their grasp, dozens of consumers grabbed it with both hands.

Liza: I even cried I was so emotional. I’m getting this wonderful car. I never thought I would be driving a BMW.

V/O: But sheer driving pleasure turned to anxious despair: the deal seems to have been built on a Ponzi scheme disguised as affordable vehicle finance.

QSG Consult was run by father and son Johan and Riaan Smit out of this house in Benoni. They were supposedly trading in oil in Dubai, and motorists who would never normally be able to afford a BMW, could now buy one if they invested in QSG, and earn massive returns to cover their monthly instalments.

But when the Asset Forfeiture Unit froze QSG’s bank accounts last year, it put an end to any investment return payments. After apparently fleecing investors of 370 million, the Smits fled to Dubai. Forensic investigator Chad Thomas has been investigating since 2017.

Chad: A lot of people were then told: listen, there’s a helluva deal to be made. You can now buy a car that QSG will pay for, and part of the finance deal that you have with the finance house or the motor dealership will be able to have a surplus amount invested into QSG. So, not just are you getting a car, but QSG will pay for your car every month and you’ll get returns on your money, because there will be surplus money on the finance deal of that particular motor vehicle.

V/O: The deal was marketed by QSG Sales Manager Daanie Delportt. This charismatic Christian is also a gospel singer.

Daanie: “Ek ken ‘n naam, dit is kosbaar ver bo alles.”

V/O: He spread the word, and people flocked to the participating dealership: BMW Melrose Arch. The Dealer Principal was Madelyn Coburn; and the salesman Justin Lineveldt.

Justin: “It’s a company called QSG that I’ve been doing their business for. I’ve been doing their business now for about 18 months, okay. So what I do is I will build a deal on a new car to get you out as much money as possible. That money then earns you obviously your returns every month. So all you’re doing here is taking the bank’s money and getting it to subsidize your car, if that makes sense, to try and get your repayment as small as possible. So there’s nothing illegal, the only catch is obviously you must have a trade-in. You can’t get money out of the deal without a trade-in.

Devi: Did it seem like a really good deal?

Riaan: It’s a fantastic deal. I bought 3 BMWs and they actually were going to pay me R500 to drive the cars.

Devi: So you traded in 3 vehicles. So what was the value of the Atos?

Riaan: R160 000 more or less, and the i10 they gave R177 000.

V/O: Justin was offering more on the trade-ins, than they cost brand-new.

Riaan: We questioned him about that and he said don’t worry, that is how it’s formulated.

Liza: Obviously we didn’t really worry about this because we are getting BMWs.

V/O: Derek Harmse flew up from Richards Bay to collect his new X4 from Justin. Melrose Arch gave him R314 000 trade-in on his old 5 series, but never collected it. Here he is with new and old BMW in Richard’s Bay last week.

This woman’s invoice reflected a trade-in of R263 000 for a Chevrolet bakkie, she never even told them about. In fact, it had been written off the year before.

V/O: Riaan and Liza bought an X4 and two 120i’s for their kids. They paid a total of two point three million rand – totally inflated, according to Chad.

Chad: You’re buying a car for half a million rand, but that car’s getting financed for 800 or 900 000 rand. So, you’re talking about a car being loaded by almost double its value. How is it being loaded? Well, they are loading things that are supposedly extras on the vehicle, perhaps those extras aren’t even supplied. They are charging you for some things that are already on that vehicle, but it’s just to get that surplus money out of that particular deal.

V/O: Customers paid hundreds of thousands for so-called extras, including standard items like dynamic brake lights, Bluetooth and audio interface. Riaan’s three cars were financed by Wesbank and BMW Financial Services at inflated prices, and the surplus or cash-back was given to him to invest in QSG.

Devi: They gave you R600 000?

Riaan: BMW gave me R600 000. I must open a Mercantile Bank account and I must pay it back it back into the Mercantile account and they will put it into QSG.

V/O: The finance houses paid BMW Melrose Arch who then paid customers’ cash-backs into Mercantile Bank accounts. This was transferred to QSG in Dubai, who paid 6% interest per month back into Mercantile Bank to cover the monthly instalments.

Devi: So, you were going to pay R40 000 a month for three BMWs?

Riaan: Yes.

Devi: And how much was going to come into your bank account?

Riaan: R42 000.

Devi: They were paying you?

Liza: Yes, we were even going to get a little bit more out.

V/O: Justin Lineveldt told Riaan that his deal was just one of many.

Riaan: He showed me actually that day that they’ve done already 150 deals that month.

Link: Fourteen of the BMW drivers had their cars financed by Wesbank. Wesbank told us that they aren’t aware of any other cases through this special Melrose Arch deal. They were unwilling to give us an on-camera interview.

V/O: Anthony Allen also bought an X4 and an X1 through this special Justin deal.

Devi: Did you have any concerns?

Anthony: I had my reservations in the beginning, but I phoned around.

V/O: Anthony even consulted the Dealer Principal, Madelyn Coburn, for reassurance.

Anthony: Hi Madelyn.

Madelyn: Yes.

Anthony: Hi, it’s Anthony speaking.

Madelyn: Yes.

Anthony: I’m dealing with Justin on a potential deal with regards to a vehicle at your branch

Madelyn: Yes

Anthony: And I just want to pick your brain if you don’t mind. It’s that alternative, or subsidized funding package that you guys are offering.

Madelyn: Yes.

Anthony: I wanted to find out just the interactions that you’ve had, the stability of it, and your findings in that regard?

Madelyn: We’ve had no issues at all. You know I’m not directly involved with it. It’s done through my, through Melrose Arch, we’ve had absolutely no issues at all.

Anthony: Okay. And you’ve had multiple purchases…on that deal?

Madelyn: Many, many, many, on exactly that basis. Absolutely, many. Hundreds.

Anthony: No hiccups whatsoever thus far?

Madelyn: None at all.

Anthony: Okay, no great.

Madelyn: And Justin’s been here for 8 months, and I’ve never had one customer phone me and say what’s you know, what’s the story?

V/O: BMW Melrose Arch has closed down, but we managed to track Madelyn Coburn on the phone.

Devi: We’re doing the story on Sunday. Your name has been mentioned, and the allegation is that you were aware of this Ponzi scheme. In fact you endorsed it.

Madelyn: Devi, the truth of the matter is not at all.

Devi: So, you didn’t know about it?

Madelyn: I’m not saying I didn’t know about it. I said I didn’t endorse it at all.

Devi: So, you did know about it?

Madelyn: I didn’t say I knew about it, I’m saying I didn’t endorse it at all.

Devi: Did you try and stop it?

Madelyn: Yes, absolutely.

Devi: Were you successful?

Madelyn: Yes, absolutely.

Devi: But hundreds of cars had already been sold at that time, in your own words?

Madelyn: No, not at all.

Devi: In your own words?

Madelyn: That’s not true.

Devi: No, it is true.

V/O: Anthony’s instalments are over R37 000 a month, and he’s had to take out a second bond on his home. He only signed the Offer-To-Purchase on the day he collected the cars, but never realized his income and expenditure figures had been altered on the application form to BMW Finance.

Anthony: On one of the applications my salary actually had doubled more or less, and my expenses halved.

V/O: Shaheeda Moosa also bought two cars through BMW Melrose Arch. Her payments are R30 000 a month, but she claims she never signed an Offer-To-Purchase.

Shaheeda: BMW Financial, when I asked them to send me all documents where I ordered this car, the OTP, they couldn’t send me an unsigned document. They sent me that. Immediately I noticed my signature was compromised there.

Devi: This is not your signature?

Shaheeda: No, no that is not my signature.

V/O: The only document she ever signed was an application form a week before, and the difference is obvious.

Shaheeda: I sent BMW Financial Services an email telling them I didn’t sign that document. They just avoided me and ignored me. They were not interested in helping.

Link: Many of the cars bought under the QSG cash-back deal were financed through BMW Financial Services. BMW South Africa is handling those queries. They’ve been aware of the situation for some time yet told us they were still investigating.

V/O: BMW South Africa warned their dealer network about the Ponzi scheme in October 2017 and told them not to get involved in illegal schemes. In a written statement, BMW says: “We have profound sympathy for anyone who has fallen foul of the apparent collapse of QSG Consult. Our brand has also been tarnished by association with this matter. BMW Financial Services and BMW South Africa are separate legal entities to Hyde Park Auto trading as Melrose Arch Auto.”

V/O: Melrose Arch may have closed down, but Justin Lineveldt continued selling BMWs. He refused an interview and sent us a written statement.

V/O: “In connection with your question as to how the scheme worked, I am not in a position to give the facts on this as I worked for BMW selling cars, not the company in question. This you would have to get from the clients or the people that referred them to me and I was not present in any of their discussions to have the facts as to what was presented to them. There were never any agreements between BMW or QSG, I was simply servicing their clients with new vehicles as requested by the clients when they contacted me.”

V/O: But what about Daanie Delportt?

Danie: You gotta rebuke the spirit of poverty over your life!

V/O: This part-time preacher cancelled his interview, but returned our phone call:

Devi: How many people called you in all those years that you referred to Melrose Arch?

Daanie: Do you want me to take a thumb suck?

Devi: Yes, was it ten, twenty, a hundred? How many people called you?

Daanie: I would say a hundred people called me, easily a hundred people.

V/O: Daanie Delportt confirmed that he earned a million rand a month from QSG. But Prishen Ramsamy cannot make the R15 000 monthly instalment on his BMW, and has now been blacklisted.

Link: The reality is the customers who did get involved believed it was a bona fide deal, signed and sealed under the auspices of a BMW dealership.

V/O: The Director of BMW Melrose Arch is Justin Divaris. He too refused an interview, and in a written statement says “We have not been the only victim of the alleged QSG Ponzi Scheme which appears to have affected multiple industries and channels, including vehicle dealerships. Melrose Arch Auto in no way encouraged or recommended to any person to invest in QSG. Any allegations of improper conduct or fraudulent activity are entirely unfounded, and denied in the strongest terms.

V/O: Anthony’s instalments are over R37 000 a month, and he’s had to take out a second bond on his home. He only signed the Offer-To-Purchase on the day he collected the cars, but never realized his income and expenditure figures had been altered on the application form to BMW Finance. Anthony: On one of the applications my salary actually had doubled more or less, and my expenses halved. V/O: Shaheeda Moosa also bought two cars through BMW Melrose Arch. Her payments are R30 000 a month, but she claims she never signed an Offer-To-Purchase. Shaheeda: BMW Financial, when I asked them to send me all documents where I ordered this car, the OTP, they couldn’t send me an unsigned document. They sent me that. Immediately I noticed my signature was compromised there. Devi: This is not your signature? Shaheeda: No, no that is not my signature. V/O: The only document she ever signed was an application form a week before, and the difference is obvious. Shaheeda: I sent BMW Financial Services an email telling them I didn’t sign that document. They just avoided me and ignored me. They were not interested in helping. Link: Many of the cars bought under the QSG cash-back deal were financed through BMW Financial Services. BMW South Africa is handling those queries. They’ve been aware of the situation for some time yet told us they were still investigating. V/O: BMW South Africa warned their dealer network about the Ponzi scheme in October 2017 and told them not to get involved in illegal schemes. In a written statement, BMW says: “We have profound sympathy for anyone who has fallen foul of the apparent collapse of QSG Consult. Our brand has also been tarnished by association with this matter. BMW Financial Services and BMW South Africa are separate legal entities to Hyde Park Auto trading as Melrose Arch Auto.” V/O: Melrose Arch may have closed down, but Justin Lineveldt continued selling BMWs. He refused an interview and sent us a written statement. V/O: “In connection with your question as to how the scheme worked, I am not in a position to give the facts on this as I worked for BMW selling cars, not the company in question. This you would have to get from the clients or the people that referred them to me and I was not present in any of their discussions to have the facts as to what was presented to them. There were never any agreements between BMW or QSG, I was simply servicing their clients with new vehicles as requested by the clients when they contacted me.” V/O: But what about Daanie Delportt? Danie: You gotta rebuke the spirit of poverty over your life! V/O: This part-time preacher cancelled his interview, but returned our phone call: Devi: How many people called you in all those years that you referred to Melrose Arch? Daanie: Do you want me to take a thumb suck? Devi: Yes, was it ten, twenty, a hundred? How many people called you? Daanie: I would say a hundred people called me, easily a hundred people. V/O: Daanie Delportt confirmed that he earned a million rand a month from QSG. But Prishen Ramsamy cannot make the R15 000 monthly instalment on his BMW, and has now been blacklisted. Link: The reality is the customers who did get involved believed it was a bona fide deal, signed and sealed under the auspices of a BMW dealership. V/O: The Director of BMW Melrose Arch is Justin Divaris. He too refused an interview, and in a written statement says “We have not been the only victim of the alleged QSG Ponzi Scheme which appears to have affected multiple industries and channels, including vehicle dealerships. Melrose Arch Auto in no way encouraged or recommended to any person to invest in QSG. Any allegations of improper conduct or fraudulent activity are entirely unfounded, and denied in the strongest terms. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): How did BMW Melrose Arch sell dozens of luxury cars through a Ponzi scheme?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: According to the Dealer Principal BMW Melrose Arch sold "hundreds" of cars through a dodgy cash back, dealer assist scheme which was linked to a non-existent oil company in Dubai. If customers were creditworthy and had a trade-in, their new, luxury cars would pay for themselves. When the Reserve Bank identified QSG as a Ponzi scheme and the Asset Forfeiture Unit froze R71 million in QSG's funds, the hundreds of BMW owners were no longer able to make the exorbitant payments on their new cars.
metadata.Summary: This "special offer" was only available through BMW Melrose Arch, and only one salesman was doing the deals: Justin Lineveldt. The scheme involved inflating the invoices for the car finance by as much as possible. Trade-ins were marked up to three times their value, extras were charged for on paper, but not added to the cars; the higher the finance amount, the higher the "cash-back" deal. The "cash-back" portion was then invested in QSG, which was ostensibly doing business with an oil company in Dubai. The so-called interest on this investment would then be paid to an account at Mercantile Bank, which would then make the car payments at Wesbank or BMW Auto Finance.
metadata.Further information: The cash-back deal was the brainchild of Daanie Delportt, a former second-hand car dealer who bought a car through Justin Lineveldt. Daanie became the self-styled Marketing Director for QSG and found hundreds of potential customers which he sent to Justin at Melrose Arch. On asking the Melrose Arch Dealer Principal if the deal was legitimate, customers were given reassurance that nothing was wrong. Daanie is also a part-time Christian preacher who convinced several customers that the Lord was on their side and rewarding them with this special deal. BMW Melrose Arch has recently closed down, but was owned by Justin Divaris - owner of BMW Hyde Auto and BMW Sandton Isle. Justin is building an 8000m2 "candy store for supercars" in Melrose Arch. This R2 billion building will include Rolls Royce, Aston Martin, McLaren and a Marriott Hotel. This means the Sandton Isle site will become a BMW super centre.
